title: Grid-Scale Battery Storage — Competitive Assessment
topic: Grid-scale battery energy storage systems — the head-to-head set of system suppliers and integrators

scope.rationale: The `storage-integrators-and-containers` segment as the registry holds it on the day — ten incumbents and eight challengers (18) — plus `flexgen`, kept as the named adjacent comparator the pure-integrator consolidation judgment needs (19). The rule, not the list, is the scope, and it is re-derived for each edition: it grew from twelve hand-cut names at the 2026-08-29 edition to nineteen here, adding eight and dropping one. `eve-energy` leaves because the registry places it in cells and in-hall power rather than in the integrator set — its Mr.Giant block is a cell maker's system line. The segment's other adjacent members — the gen-set OEMs, Vertiv, Eaton, GE Vernova, Huawei Digital Power, Narada, ON.energy and Sinexcel — stay out because they sell into the integration business rather than compete in it.

gaps: All revenue comparisons are **whole-company**, not BESS-segment — no company in scope discloses BESS revenue comparably. A company-level figure overstates BESS scale for diversified groups (storage is a single-digit share of BYD and Tesla revenue) and is the whole business only for pure plays like Fluence. H1 2026 made this worse rather than better: BYD's interim confirms storage is still inside 'automobiles and related products' with no GWh anywhere in the filing.

**Eight of nineteen carry no normalized figure**, each for a stated reason: Wärtsilä (storage reclassified pending the RCT JV), HyperStrong (public and growing but no USD overlay carried), Trina Storage (segment not broken out of the parent), CRRC Zhuzhou (business unit of a listed parent, BU profitability undisclosed), Envision Energy, LS Energy Solutions, Prevalon and FlexGen (private or subsidiary, no standalone financials). They appear with the reason rather than with a manufactured number.

**No H1 2026 figure enters the normalized table.** Neither Sungrow's, BYD's nor any other H1 print carries a sourced CNY/USD rate in its dossier, and the schema forbids an unsourced conversion — so the comparison stays on the last full fiscal year while the narrative carries the halves.
Hithium's comparable figure is FY2024, from its HKEX listing prospectus — no FY2025 full-year figure is publicly filed after three failed listing attempts.

**Rankings in this report are reproduced as the dossiers cite them and are not reconciled**, because they cannot be: Benchmark, Wood Mackenzie and InfoLink disagree on the FY2025 integrator order, Wood Mackenzie's own two 2025 instruments disagree with each other, and none states its metric precisely enough to explain the gap. The ranking-basis table records the instrument for each claim.

This report is built from the covered dossiers alone: no fresh research was performed for it, and no field-note content appears in it. Sourcing quality is bounded by each dossier's own source list. The `byd` and `eve-energy` dossiers were refreshed to their H1 2026 interims immediately before this edition was authored; every other dossier is pinned as it stood.

bluf: **BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** The grid-scale integrator contest is nineteen companies, not twelve, and the eight added on the registry's own roster include a Wood Mackenzie top-five name the previous cut omitted entirely [c:c37]. Scale leadership still sits with vertically integrated Chinese cell-owners, but H1 2026 broke the link between company scale and storage performance: BYD was ranked first in system-integrator shipments by two independent counts while its group profit fell 20.54%, and Sungrow's storage line carried exactly half its revenue while both the line and the company shrank [c:c31] [c:c30] [c:c3]. Meanwhile every listed Chinese peer whose storage business is visible as a segment grew profit sharply in the same half [c:c33]. The read: whole-company revenue — the only figure comparable across this set — is now actively misleading about storage, and the pure-integrator tier continues to consolidate out of independence rather than into it.

keyJudgments.text: **(High confidence)** We assess the peer set must be taken from the registry rather than hand-cut, and that the previous cut materially under-counted the field. Eight covered companies selling grid-scale BESS at system level sat outside the 2026-08-29 scope, among them Envision Energy — tied fifth on the only comprehensive global integrator scorecard published — and CRRC Zhuzhou, which leads APAC regional share. Basis: the `storage-integrators-and-containers` roster on the day, against the prior edition's twelve.

**(High confidence)** We assess company scale and storage performance have decoupled, and that H1 2026 is the print that demonstrates it. BYD holds the H1 2026 integrator crown on two independent counts while its group profit fell 20.54% on a RMB 8.34B adverse finance-expense swing; Sungrow's ESS reached exactly 50.00% of revenue while group revenue fell 28.99% and the storage line itself fell 13.18%. Basis: both interims as filed, plus Benchmark and InfoLink shipment counts.

**(High confidence)** We assess no ordinal ranking in this market should be cited without its instrument. Benchmark ranks BYD #1 for FY2025 while Wood Mackenzie and InfoLink rank it #3; Wood Mackenzie's own market-share and scorecard instruments place BYD differently in the same year; and none of the three states its metric precisely enough to reconcile. Basis: the three rankings as the dossiers carry them. This is a claim about the evidence, not about the companies.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess the pure-integrator tier is consolidating out of independence. Wärtsilä has moved storage into a 50/50 JV and stopped reporting it as a segment, Prevalon was acquired by Nextpower for up to $365M, and FlexGen converted Powin's assets into a 25+ GWh software-and-services fleet rather than an integration business. Basis: three completed transactions in eighteen months. The survivors in that tier lead on provenance — US-made or Korean cells — rather than on scale.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess the storage cycle turned favourably in H1 2026 for companies whose storage is visible, and that the turn is priced in volume rather than margin. Utility-scale cell prices recovered quarter-on-quarter from a price-war floor near RMB 0.30/Wh, and every listed Chinese peer with a storage segment grew profit — but the margin gap between the leader and the second tier is wide (CATL 23.96% storage gross margin against EVE's 12.51%), which is the second tier paying for volume with price. Basis: the interim review of the listed Chinese BESS players.

sections.title: What changed since the last edition
sections.read: The corpus movement that made this edition necessary, before any of it is interpreted.
ps: **The peer set is the registry's, and it is nineteen.** The 2026-08-29 edition cut the field at twelve on a hand-drawn "cell-to-system suppliers and pure integrators" rule. This edition takes the `storage-integrators-and-containers` segment as the registry holds it on the day — ten incumbents and eight challengers — plus FlexGen as the named adjacent comparator the consolidation judgment needs. Eleven names carry over. **Eight are added**: Envision Energy, CRRC Zhuzhou, HyperStrong, Trina Storage, Jinko, Sunwoda, LS Energy Solutions and Prevalon. **One leaves**: EVE Energy, which the registry places in cells and in-hall power rather than in the integrator set — its Mr.Giant block is a cell maker's system line, and its H1 2026 filing reports storage as a battery segment rather than an integration business [c:c45], and the cell rankers that place it second or third globally are counting cells, not systems [c:c34]. The omissions mattered: Envision is tied fifth on Wood Mackenzie's 2026 integrator ranking [c:c37] and was outside the old scope entirely.

**Sungrow's H1 2026 is the print that dates the last edition.** Revenue fell 28.99% to RMB 30.912B and attributable profit 32.01% to RMB 5.259B, while gross margin *rose* 1.56pp to 35.92% [c:c3]. Inside that, energy storage carried the company for the first time — ESS systems RMB 15.456B, exactly 50.00% of revenue, on 25 GWh of H1 shipments — but the storage line itself fell 13.18% and its gross margin gave up 7.49pp to 32.43% [c:c3] [c:c4]. Overseas held far better than home: mainland China -54.71%, overseas +/-10.59%. The prior edition's Judgment 1 rested on Sungrow's mix shift into storage; the mix shift is confirmed and the revenue is down by nearly a third.

**BYD's H1 2026 landed, and it inverts the frame.** Group revenue fell 7.13% to RMB 344.815B and attributable profit 20.54% to RMB 12.325B, with a RMB 8.34B adverse swing in finance expenses that is on its own about 2.6 times the fall in profit [c:c44] [c:c30]. Yet on shipments BYD is first: Benchmark puts it at 9.1% of 313 GWh of H1 system-integrator shipments and InfoLink also ranks it first, a ranking BYD cites in its own interim [c:c31] [c:c44]. The two facts sit together because BYD discloses no storage segment at all — the interim's only structural change was renaming the handset segment, and storage stays inside "automobiles and related products" with no GWh figure anywhere in the filing [c:c44].

**The FY2025 integrator crown is disputed, not merely scope-dependent — and the last edition did not say so.** Benchmark ranks BYD first for 2025 at 60 GWh and 13% share; Wood Mackenzie and InfoLink both rank Tesla first, Sungrow second and BYD third [c:c32]. Wood Mackenzie's own two 2025 instruments differ from each other — third on market share, fourth on the ten-criteria scorecard [c:c37] — which is a difference of instrument, not a contradiction, but reads as one when cited side by side without the basis. None of the rankers states its metric precisely enough to explain the gap, and no source reconciles them. This edition therefore carries the basis in a table of its own rather than a single ordinal.

**And the half was good for everyone except the diversified.** Every listed Chinese BESS peer with a pure-play storage line grew profit sharply in H1 2026 — CATL +41.98% with storage revenue +87.54% at a 23.96% gross margin, EVE +105.66% with storage +69.15% at 12.51%, CALB, Gotion, Great Power, REPT and Desay all up in triple digits or from losses — against utility-scale cell prices recovering quarter-on-quarter from a price-war floor near RMB 0.30/Wh [c:c33]. BYD's group profit fell 20.54% in the same half, and Sungrow's fell 32.01%. The divergence is not about storage demand; it is about what else is in the P&L.

sections.title: The competitive read
ps: **The field is wider than the last edition showed, and the widening is concentrated in one tier.** Of the eight companies added, six are Chinese and none is small: Envision is tied fifth on the only comprehensive integrator scorecard published, CRRC Zhuzhou leads APAC regional share, HyperStrong is top-five on shipments under one instrument and invisible under two others. Wood Mackenzie puts Chinese integrators at 76% of the global market [c:c32]. A head-to-head that omitted three of them was not measuring the contest.

**Scale and storage performance have come apart, and H1 2026 is where it shows.** The two largest balance sheets in the table — BYD and Tesla — are the two whose storage results are least observable, because neither reports storage as a segment a reader can check. BYD's group profit fell 20.54% in a half when it was ranked first in integrator shipments by two independent counts [c:c30] [c:c31]; every pure-play or near-pure-play listed Chinese peer grew profit sharply in the same half [c:c33]. The inference is not that BYD's storage business is weak. It is that whole-company revenue — the only figure comparable across this set — is now actively misleading about storage, and the gap is widest exactly where the numbers are largest.

**The pure-integrator tier is still consolidating, and the direction is out.** Wärtsilä is moving storage into a 50/50 JV with RCT Solutions and has stopped reporting it as a segment [c:c36]. Prevalon was acquired by Nextpower for up to $365M [c:c27]. FlexGen bought Powin's assets out of Chapter 11 and now runs 25+ GWh as software and services rather than as an integrator [c:c28]. Three of the four independents that were not vertically integrated have changed owner, changed structure, or changed business in eighteen months. The survivors in that tier are the ones with a provenance story rather than a scale story — Prevalon's US-made AESC cells through Fixx [c:c40], LS-ES's Korean parent and Korean cells [c:c43].

**What the widened field does not change.** The block race is still the frontier fight and it is still architectural, and the top of the shipment tables is still held by companies that own their cells. Adding eight names moves no incumbent out of the top tier. What it changes is the denominator — and therefore every share claim computed against the old twelve.

sections.title: The AI data-centre adjacency
ps: The integrator set is being pulled toward AI-data-centre storage from two directions at once, and the covered record is thinner than the noise suggests. On the demand side the buyers are real: BYD lists energy storage for AIDC among its served segments in its own interim [c:c44], and Envision commissioned the first building of its Galaxy Campus running on on-site renewables [c:c47]. On the supply side, the products announced into this lane are mostly announcements — Prevalon's HPS is the one in the set with DOE-laboratory validation against GPU load profiles and a named integration path [c:c40]. Treat AIDC as a lane where position is being taken and revenue is not yet visible in any company in this scope.

guidanceOverlays.title: The integrator field, as a counterparty question
ps: The integrator peer set is nineteen covered companies on the registry's own roster, and eight of them publish no comparable financials at all — private, subsidiary, or a business unit inside a listed parent. For an independent engineer that is the counterparty file in one line: for eight of nineteen there is no audited standalone statement to read, and the diligence has to run on installed base, parentage and order book instead.

The tier that has changed most is the one without vertical integration. Three of the four independents that did not own cells have changed owner, structure or business in eighteen months — one into a joint venture, one acquired outright, one converted from integration into software and services. Counterparty risk in that tier is not primarily balance-sheet risk; it is the risk that the entity signing the long-term service agreement is not the entity that will perform it.

guidanceOverlays.title: Where the integrator field actually earns
ps: Half of 2026 separated company scale from storage performance in this field. The two largest balance sheets among the integrators are also the two whose storage results cannot be checked, because neither reports storage as a segment — one of them was ranked first in global system shipments for the half by two independent counts while its group profit fell by a fifth. Every listed peer whose storage is visible as a segment grew profit sharply in the same half.

The practical consequence for reading this market: whole-company revenue is the only figure comparable across the field, and it is now actively misleading about storage. Ask which market design a supplier's volume is actually earning in, and whether its storage line is visible at all, before treating group scale as evidence of storage strength.
